description: Found by defk-9p6.12 (examples/ws_masking.exs). A kernel that implements a behaviour callback (Bandit.PrimitiveOps.WebSocket.ws_mask/2) cannot carry @impl true: written before the defk, the attribute attaches to the first function the macro generates, __defk_load__/0, and Elixir warns 'got @impl true for __defk_load__/0 but no behaviour specifies such callback'. The kernel still satisfies the behaviour, so the example leaves @impl out (noted in its header). Done when @impl (true or a behaviour module) before a defk applies to the kernel's public function and the generated helpers carry none, with a test that a behaviour-implementing kernel compiles without warnings under --warnings-as-errors.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** `@impl` written before a `defk` applies to the kernel's public function, not to the generated `__defk_load__/0`

**Current behavior (reproduced in triage):**

    defmodule M do
      use Defk
      @behaviour B            # @callback mask(integer, integer) :: integer
      @impl true
      defk mask(a :: i64, b :: i64) :: i64, do: bxor(a, b)
    end

warns `got "@impl true" for function __defk_load__/0 but no behaviour specifies such callback. The known callbacks are: B.mask/2`. The kernel still works and satisfies the behaviour, but code under --warnings-as-errors cannot use @impl (examples/ws_masking.exs leaves it out and says so).

**Desired behavior:**
`@impl true` or `@impl SomeBehaviour` placed before a `defk` (single-clause or the head of a multi-clause kernel) attaches to that kernel's public function `name/arity`; no generated function (`__defk_load__/0` and the other `__defk_*` helpers, Elixir-mode functions) carries an @impl. Elixir's usual @impl checks then apply to the kernel (e.g. once any @impl is used, other callbacks without @impl warn as in plain Elixir).

**Key interfaces:**
- `defk` macro expansion and the order of the functions `Defk.__before_compile__/1` emits
- examples/ws_masking.exs header note

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A module implementing a behaviour with `@impl true` before a defk compiles with no warnings under --warnings-as-errors and the callback is recognised
- [ ] `@impl B` (module form) works the same
- [ ] A multi-clause kernel with @impl before its head works
- [ ] `@impl true` before a defk that matches no callback gives Elixir's normal warning naming the kernel, not `__defk_load__/0`
- [ ] examples/ws_masking.exs uses `@impl true` and drops the note; `mix test`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- @doc/@spec handling for kernels (unchanged)
- Generating behaviour callbacks automatically

title: @impl true before a defk attaches to __defk_load__/0, not the kernel
